newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline sags again amid poor local, US demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline sags again amid poor local, US demand.

text.p: NWE gasoline was slightly weaker on Thursday, under pressure from sagging screen values, traders said.

A trader bought Eurograde barges in the morning at $190 and $189 fob ARA but prices then fell back. A refiner sold running refinery material in the afternoon at $186.50 and $188 fob Antwerp, and another refiner bought regular gasoline barges at $180.50.

Dealers said they felt weakness in the U.S. had kept arbitrage opportunities unworkable for the time being and said by the day's end that Europe's prices needed to fall by at least five dollars a tonne relative to those in the U.S. for more material to be sold westwards.

This put further pressure on European prices and although local demand was slack and fixed price discussion was not heard, cif cargo numbers were thought to have slipped down more or less towards barge levels.
Some discussions were heard for catgas and reformate blending components but prices for these were also not known.
